To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the alcohol consumption and the number of alcohol-related problems are higher in Sweden than in the Baltic countries and Italy; that the risk-curve analyses showed that the risk of alcohol problems increases with increasing consumption; and that the risk-curved analyses showed that the alcohol-related problems were more common among the Swedish respondents than the respondents from the other countries.

1) the risk of alcohol dependence was higher for those who started drinking at an earlier age and who drank heavily; 2) those who had been drinking for a longer time had a higher risk of alcohol dependence; and 3) the risk of dependence was higher among males than females and among those who had a family history of alcohol dependence.
the prevalence of alcohol use disorders is high, and that the prevalence of heavy drinking is high among those who do not have an alcohol use disorder.

a comparative analysis of the alcohol consumption patterns and alcohol-related problems in five European countries, namely, Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania, Sweden and Italy.

the evidence for the association between alcohol consumption and the development of alcohol dependence is not strong enough to draw firm conclusions.
alcohol use is associated with an increased risk of breast cancer, but the evidence is not sufficient to establish a causal relationship.

alcohol consumption is a risk factor for cancer of the oral cavity and pharynx and the larynx, as well as for cancers of the oesophagus and the liver, and that it is probably a risk factor for cancers of the colorectum, breast (in postmenopausal women), and the pancreas, but not for cancer of the stomach, and that it may be a risk factor for the development of cancers at other sites.

the alcohol-related problems in the Baltic countries are higher than in Sweden and Italy, but not higher than in other countries in the European Union.

there are no significant differences in the alcohol consumption patterns between the Baltic countries.
the risk of developing alcohol dependence is strongly associated with the amount of alcohol that is consumed.
